_how_to_read: Each step holds the exact JSON sent and received; the _request_notes/_response_notes beside it annotate every top-level field (and the top-level fields of result).
where_the_model_runs: The model call happens in the host, in week9/agent/loop.py (model.complete), after tools/list returns and before tools/call is sent; it never happens on this wire or inside the ticket-history server, which only lists tools and executes them.

http._note: 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. Remote MCP auth sits in HTTP, under JSON-RPC: the request is refused before any MCP method runs.

_request_notes.jsonrpc: Always the string "2.0": this is JSON-RPC 2.0 framing.
_request_notes.id: Request id chosen by the client; would be echoed in the response.
_request_notes.method: initialize -- but it never reaches MCP: the HTTP layer rejects it first.
_request_notes.params: Same params as step 1. Irrelevant here; auth is checked before parsing.

_response_notes.(empty body): No JSON-RPC response at all: no token, no session, no id echoed.

http._note: The response header mcp-session-id names this session; every later request must send it back.

_request_notes.id: 1 -- the first request of the session; the response carries the same id.
_request_notes.method: initialize: the handshake. Nothing else may be sent before it.
_request_notes.params: protocolVersion the client speaks, the client's capabilities (none offered: no sampling, no roots), and clientInfo (who is calling).

result.instructions: Support Ops ticket history. Look tickets up by id (TCK-nnnn). Records are read-only.

_response_notes.id: 1 -- matches the request, which is how the client pairs them.
_response_notes.result: The server's half of the handshake (fields below).
_response_notes.result.protocolVersion: The version the server agreed to; both sides now speak it.
_response_notes.result.capabilities: What this server offers: tools, resources and prompts (each with listChanged notifications), logging, plus experimental/extensions slots. The host only asks for what is listed here.
_response_notes.result.serverInfo: Name and version of the server -- ticket-history 1.3.0. This is the third-party identity the risk note is about.
_response_notes.result.instructions: Free text the server wants the host to show its model. Untrusted input from a third party, like any tool description.

http._note: 202 Accepted with an empty body. Only now may the client send requests.

_request_notes.method: notifications/initialized: the client confirms the handshake is done.
_request_notes.(no id): No id field at all -- that is what makes it a notification: no reply.

_request_notes.method: tools/list: discovery. The answer is the ONLY source of the agent's tool list for this server.
_request_notes.params: Empty: no pagination cursor on the first page.

tools.name: get_ticket
tools.description:
Fetch one support ticket by id: subject, status, priority, product area,
the customer's own message and how many times it was escalated.

Use it whenever the user names a ticket id (ids look like TCK-nnnn, e.g.
TCK-4403). It does not search: if you only have a description of the
problem, do not guess an id.

tools.name: get_escalation_history
tools.description:
Every escalation behind a ticket (TCK-nnnn), oldest first: when, from
which tier to which, who moved it and why.

The host usually attaches this as context already (resource
tickets://{ticket_id}/escalations); only call it when that context is not
in the conversation.

_response_notes.result.tools: One entry per tool: name, description (the docstring the model reads as a prompt), inputSchema (JSON Schema the model's arguments must satisfy), outputSchema, annotations (readOnlyHint), and _meta. Two tools: get_ticket, get_escalation_history.

_request_notes.method: tools/call: execute one tool. The model chose it, in the host, before this request was written.
_request_notes.params: name (the server's own tool name, without the host's "ticket-history__" prefix) and arguments (the model's input).

content.text: {"subject":"Proration charged twice after mid-cycle upgrade","customer":{"account":"BLUE-0412","name":"Bluefin Analytics","contact_email":"finance@bluefin.example"},"status":"escalated","priority":"urgent","product_area":"subscriptions","opened_at":"2026-09-27T10:21:00Z","message":"We upgraded seats mid-cycle during the migration window and were charged the proration twice.","ticket_id":"TCK-4403","escalation_count":2,"latest_escalation":{"at":"2026-09-28T16:30:00Z","from_tier":"L2-billing","to_tier":"L3-ledger-eng","by":"agent:dana","reason":"dual-write produced two proration events; needs ledger engineering"}}

structuredContent.subject: Proration charged twice after mid-cycle upgrade
structuredContent.message: We upgraded seats mid-cycle during the migration window and were charged the proration twice.

latest_escalation.reason: dual-write produced two proration events; needs ledger engineering

_response_notes.result: The tool's output (fields below). Plain data -- no model ran.
_response_notes.result.content: Content blocks for the model: one text block holding the ticket as JSON. This is what goes into the tool_result.
_response_notes.result.structuredContent: The same record as a JSON object, typed by the tool's outputSchema, for code rather than the model.

http._note: 200 -- a tool error is not an HTTP or JSON-RPC error.

_request_notes.params: A malformed id, TCK-44, as a model might copy it from a message.

content.text: ticket id 'TCK-44' is malformed: ticket ids look like TCK-nnnn (TCK- then four digits, e.g. TCK-4401). Re-read the id from the customer's message; do not retry this exact value.

_response_notes.result: Still a RESULT, not a JSON-RPC error: the protocol worked, the tool failed. That is what lets the model see and fix it.
_response_notes.result.content: The error text the model reads: it says the id is malformed, what ids look like, and not to retry this value.
_response_notes.result.isError: true: tells the host this tool_result is an error (sent to Claude as is_error).
